summary: This article explains what makes Mercury, the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun, a world of fast years, long days, extreme temperatures, and hidden ice.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Mercury: The Closest Planet” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: the curved path an object in space follows around another object
the layer of gases around a planet
how hot or cold something is

challengeTerms.def: the line where the land or sea seems to meet the sky
one complete spin of an object around its center
very great or very far from what is normal

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that mercury would be an exciting place for people to explore in person? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Mercury is close to the Sun, yet it has ice.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review orbit, atmosphere, and temperature, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use horizon, rotation, and extreme in a short paragraph that teaches the class one of the terms with their own example.
